data.long_meaning: In Roman mythology, Tarsicium was believed to be a Roman soldier who was the tenth man in a legion led by Jupiter. His name was derived from Tarsus, a city in southern Anatolia, and the Roman god Jupiter. The name Tarsicio carries the meaning “Jupiter's tenth man” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Tarsicio usually hope their child will grow to embody jupiter's tenth man and live with faith, good character and purpose.
